question: Which mechanisms can maintain an extended H(n=2) absorbing reservoir without making its H-alpha source as bright as the inner emitting region?
starting_evidence: The preceding cause study found a descriptive difference between the original free model and the saved physical atmosphere. No matched-geometry causal attribution has been established.
requirements: Distinguish n=2 population, n=3/n=2 source ratio, total density, emissivity, optical depth and projected area.
Identify processes already in the model before calling them additional physics.
Use the saved physical state's actual rate and pressure scales, recovering omitted diagnostic receiving PI/RR terms where needed.
Separate frozen-bath population response, dimensional force/column estimates and literature plausibility from coupled statistical/thermal/dynamical equilibrium.
A thicker extended shell can also emit off the planetary limb; it is not automatically a darker unresolved line core.
Neither a population-rate experiment nor a transit model establishes the observed emission residual as a calibrated physical signal.
parallel_investigations: Atomic population budgets and competition between excitation, photoionization, recombination/cascade and collisions.
Density, flow topology, magnetic confinement and clumping constraints.
Selective irradiation/shielding, nonlocal pumping, redistribution and angular geometry.
Root synthesis of source/opacity/projected-area requirements and the minimum discriminating follow-up.
scope: No new full atmosphere root, observational fit, production likelihood or acceptance threshold. Small diagnostic helpers and primary-source notes only.
